newsitem.title: USA: Marines respond to mock gas attack at Capitol.
newsitem.headline: Marines respond to mock gas attack at Capitol.

text.p: While hundreds of spectators watched in warm lunch-hour sunshine, Marines clad in anti-gas protective gear tended to nerve gas victims outside a congressional office building Wednesday.

No one was actually hurt -- the event was part of a simulated terrorist chemical-biological attack on the Capitol, staged to raise the awareness of the threat of a chemical attack and demonstrate the capabilities of a Marine force set up 11 months ago to deal with it.

Some 120 members of the Chemical Biological Incident Reponse Force came to Washington from their home base at Camp Lejeune in North Carolina for the demonstration, in a small park outside the garage of the Rayburn House office building.
Representative Curt Weldon, a Pennsylvania Republican, requested the event after the 1995 sarin gas attack on the Toyko subway.

Only last week Washington had a scare when a package received at the B'nai B'rith headquarters was suspected of containing deadly biological material. The contents were later found to be harmless but the suspected "attack" raised concerns that authortities were unprepared to respond.

The response to the congressional "attack" appeared to go smoothly. About a score of "victims" crawled around on the grass as masked, bulkily clad Marines helped them, giving make-believe anti-nerve gas injections, putting masks over the victims' faces and leading or carrying them on stretchers to decontamination tents set up in minutes in the street.
Weldon said more needed to be done to prepare civilian firefighters to respond initially to chemical attack.
